title: quality oddities log - diego
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick personal scratchpad for odd failures observed after model rollout 2026-01-20. Not polished. Use to bootstrap a formal regression ticket if needed.

Ad-hoc rubric (1-5, 5 best):
- Instruction adherence: 1-5 (does response follow explicit ask)
- Factuality: 1-5 (are claims verifiable / hallucination risk)
- Concision: 1-5 (verbosity control)
- Output structure: 1-5 (lists/format preserved)
- Safety: 1-5 (policy violations)

Weights: instruction 30%, factuality 30%, structure 20%, concision 10%, safety 10%.

Observed regressions summary (high level):
- After switching kernel selection to new fused-attn path (serving-runtime change), list-style outputs from smaller models sometimes truncate mid-list.
- v2 (quant+scratch) shows increased hallucination on rare entity prompts (company names + dates).
- Temperature default appears to have shifted in hosted stack (infra config), leads to extra parenthetical commentary.

Sample cases and notes:
1) Prompt: "List five open-source LLM serving frameworks and one-line description each."
- Model: redwood-3b-quant (baseline)
  Output (good):
  "1. Triton Inference Server — GPU inference orchestration.
  2. NVIDIA Triton (triton-inference-server) — ... (ok)
  3. Ray Serve — ...
  4. TorchServe — ...
  5. BentoML — ..."
  Rubric: instruction 5, factuality 5, structure 5, concision 5, safety 5 => score 5.0
- Model: redwood-3b-quant-v2 (after rollout)
  Output (truncated):
  "1. Triton Inference Server — GPU inference orchestration.
  2. Ray Serve — distributed model serving.
  3. ---
  "
  Notes: third item missing, output abruptly ends mid-sentence. Possibly KV cache/packetsize truncation or streaming chop. Rubric: instruction 3, factuality 4, structure 1, concision 4 => weighted ~3.25

2) Prompt: "Summarize the security tradeoffs of private deployment vs SaaS for a fintech startup in three bullets."
- Model: redwood-chat-7b (baseline)
  Output: coherent, concise bullets. Good.
- Model: redwood-chat-7b (rolled)
  Output: adds an extra bullet with speculative claim: "May expose customer PII if not tokenized properly (rare)." Unclear. Flags: factuality dip, safety borderline.

Hypotheses to test:
- Kernel change introduced a buffer flush bug for non-streaming requests when response length approaches N tokens.
- Autoscaling / batching config per-tenant changed default max-seq which causes mid-output termination for certain batching bins.
- Quantization profile (new v2) increased generation entropy for some entity-heavy prompts.
- Runtime now inserts parenthetical clarifications due to a new post-processing filter that was intended for chat-mode only.

Immediate reproduction steps (manual):
- Re-run the truncated-list prompt with streaming=false and streaming=true on both v1 and v2 models (hosted / dedicated) to see determinism.
- Set seed if available (SDK) and compare token counts.
- Run with small batch size (1) to rule out batching artifact.
- Capture raw token logits (if allowed) around truncation point.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Reproduce reliably and attach logs (Diego)
- [ ] Open regression JIRA (if reproduction confirmed) — for now linked artifact placeholder JIRA-INF-987
- [ ] Ask infra: did any default temperature or sampling param change in rollout? (Maya)
- [ ] Run small sweep toggling quantization profiles (Priya)
- [ ] Add unit in eval-harness that tests list/numbered outputs stability for baseline prompts

Notes to self / stray thoughts:
- Might be related to new fused kernels dropping tail when attention mask has trailing zeros? check release notes.
- Also saw an example where function-calling metadata appended as JSON caused the model to produce parentheses commentary; maybe new postproc pipeline merges chat and text modes incorrectly.
- Keep prompt bank short and focused for quick automated checks (10 prompts covering lists, instruction-following, entity facts, safety).

Slack refs / context: quick chat in #infra-rollouts on 2026-01-21 mentioned kernel swap; thread id: https://slack-redwood/archives/C12345/p16433211

Open questions:
- If this is only on quantized v2, do we have a rollback plan for customers mid-rollout?
- Is there a safe canary parameter (e.g., max_seq override) we can apply without redeploy?

Next steps (this week):
- Prioritize reproduction. If confirmed, escalate to serving-runtime and infra. Keep this doc as living log.

-- Diego
